title: latency-tail-capture-and-synthetic-backfill-procedure-2024
author: Asha Patel
abstract: Playbook for capturing high-latency tail events in production traffic, synthesizing deterministic probes that reproduce tail behavior in the eval harness, and backfilling historical shadow traces for offline quant/quality analysis. Focuses on observability signals, probe generation, synthetic backfill policy, and a triage runbook for applied ML teams.
background_and_motivation: We observe intermittent 95th+ percentile latency spikes (tail events) that are costly and can correlate with quality regressions after quant or routing changes. Typical failure modes include KV-cache thrash, quantized kernel stalls, and rarely seeded memory pressure on GPU nodes. Root cause analysis is slow when spikes are ephemeral and requests are not reproducible. This playbook defines a reproducible capture -> probe synthesis -> synthetic backfill workflow so model-onboarding, quantization, and runtime teams can reproduce, validate, and fix tail regressions without impacting live traffic.
scope_and_invariants: Applies to text generation and chat endpoints served by eval-mesh and production-serving. Not in scope: unrelated network-level outages, control-plane-only incidents. Invariants: all captures must be sampled and redacted to PII policy; probes must be deterministic given seed and tokenizer version; backfill workloads must not exceed 20% of eval-fleet capacity and must be scheduled during maintenance windows unless explicitly approved.
signal_definitions: 1) Latency-tail trigger: p99 > 1.2x baseline_p99 for 5 consecutive 1-min windows OR single-request latency > 3s for short-context endpoints. 2) Quality signal: embedding cosine drift > 0.07 on monitored slices OR token-entropy change > 0.25. 3) KV-cache miss storm: cache_miss_rate increase > 10ppt for request shard. 4) Quantization suspect: runtime quant-decoded-error > 0.5% on probe samples.
capture_pipeline_overview: Steps: 1) Detection: alert from eval-mesh-alerting (rule: latency-tail trigger). 2) Live-snapshot: invoke probe-fabricator capture job (captures request headers, tokenized input, model_version, runtime_profile, kv-cache-hash, node_id, seed). 3) Redaction: automated PII redaction using redaction-service v2.0. 4) Provenance: store snapshot in snapshot-archive with tags (incident_id, slice, model, runtime). 5) Notification: create triage ticket in Regression-Triage board and attach snapshot link.
probe_generation_steps: 1) Confirm capture integrity: run `probe-validate` against snapshot-archive/<snapshot-id>. 2) Synthesize deterministic probe: `probe-fabricator synth --snapshot <id> --tokenizer v3 --seed <snapshot-seed> --output probes/<id>.json` 3) Add contextual priming: append the production prompt-prefix and system-role observed in original request. 4) Create probe metadata with: model_variant, quant_profile (if any), runtime_kernels, kv-cache-state-hash. 5) Register probe in eval-mesh as a debug-probe with low priority: `eval-mesh register --file probes/<id>.json --priority debug`.
synthetic_backfill_playbook: Purpose: reproduce tail behavior across historical windows to determine onset and frequency. Steps: 1) Select historical window: choose up to 72 hours of traffic centered on first observed tail spike. 2) Extract compatible snapshots: use snapshot-query tool `snapshot-query --tags incident:<id> --window 72h` 3) Create backfill batch: `backfill-orchestrator create --probes probes/<id>.json --window <start>:<end> --fleet-tag eval-backfill --max-concurrency 50` 4) Throttle policy: default QPS cap at 0.2x production and backfill concurrency <= 15 per model. 5) Data retention: backfill traces stored for 90 days in backfill-archive. 6) Output artifacts: per-probe response timelines, per-token latencies, kernel-time breakdown CSVs, and per-slice quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Embedding drift).
triage_runbook: When a tail capture is generated: 1) Triage lead (owner: runtime-team) verifies capture within 30 minutes; 2) If capture reproduces in eval-mesh: mark priority=canary and start focused diff (compare kernel timings and kv-cache hit profiles). 3) If not reproducible: run synthetic backfill with three seeds (original-seed, +1, -1). 4) Escalation: if p99 remains > baseline for 2 hours and probes show quant-decoding errors > 0.5%, open a cross-team incident with runtime, quant, and model-onboarding in #inc-quant-tail. 5) Rollforward/rollback guidance: prefer model variant rollback to last known-good if quality delta > 2% and latency improvement > 20%. 6) Postmortem: attach all probes, backfill outputs, and RCA draft to the incident within 7 days.
config_table:
| Parameter | Default | Acceptable range | Purpose |
|---------------------------|----------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| p99_trigger_multiplier    | 1.2            | 1.05 - 2.0            | Sensitivity for tail detection
| single_request_threshold  | 3000ms         | 1000ms - 10000ms      | Hard threshold for immediate capture
| backfill_max_concurrency  | 50             | 1 - 200               | Max concurrent probes across eval-fleet
| backfill_qps_cap          | 0.2x           | 0.05x - 1.0x          | Fraction of production QPS allowed for backfill
| probe_retention_days      | 90             | 14 - 365              | How long to keep probe artifacts
| redaction_profile         | pii-v2         | pii-v1,pii-v2,pii-off | Redaction profile used during capture
cli_examples:
1) Validate a snapshot: `probe-validate snapshot-12345 --expect-fields tokenized_input,seed,model_variant`
2) Synthesize a probe: `probe-fabricator synth --snapshot snapshot-12345 --tokenizer v3 --seed 98765 --out probes/snap-12345.json`
3) Register for eval: `eval-mesh register --file probes/snap-12345.json --priority debug --tags incident:2024-058`
4) Create a backfill batch: `backfill-orchestrator create --probes probes/snap-12345.json --window 2024-11-10T08:00:00Z:2024-11-10T20:00:00Z --max-concurrency 20 --fleet-tag eval-backfill`
5) Quick inspect latency breakdown: `latency-inspector analyze --trace backfill-archives/snap-12345 --metrics per-token,kernel-ms`
ownership_and_slos: Owners: runtime-team (primary), model-onboarding (secondary), applied-ml (observer). Contact: #runtime-ops, runtime-oncall@redwood.com. SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 420ms for short context routes; p99 <= 900ms (production baseline). Alerting thresholds: p99 > 1.2x baseline triggers capture; p99 > 1.5x baseline opens incident. Backfill SLA: initial backfill artifacts available within 4 hours of orchestration request (90% of time).
remediation_guidance: Example remediations mapped to findings: - KV-cache thrash: increase prefix cache TTL, enable sticky routing for affected tenancy, and re-run warmup probe set. - Quant kernel stalls: revert to float kernel for variant, flag quant_profile for re-tuning, schedule quant stress test on the hybrid-quant harness. - Node-level memory pressure: cordon node_id found in snapshot, redeploy model replicas to nodes with free memory > 80%. Always validate fix by re-running the synthesized probe set and a 1h backfill sample.
postincident_analysis_and_metrics: Track the following per incident: number of captures, reproduction rate in eval-mesh, mean time to first reproducible probe (MTFR) goal < 3 hours, percent incidents resolved by rollback vs code fix, and percent reduction in tail incidence after remediation. Use dashboard 'Latency Tail Index' (dash-id: LT-23) to monitor long-term trends and meta-analyses.

notes_and_future_work: Planned improvements: automated root-cause classification using probe feature vectors, tighter integration with quant-simulator to pre-run possible regressions before backfill, and a lightweight browser for probe diffs inside the console. Roadmap ticket: APPL-EVAL-522.
conclusion: This playbook provides a repeatable, low-risk path from production tail observation to offline reproducibility and remediation. Following the capture -> probe -> backfill -> triage lifecycle reduces MTTR and increases confidence for quant and model rollouts.
